transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-05-07 14:00 PDT | Duration: ~45 min | Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Jules (CSM), Maria (Lead Mobile), Tom (ML), Priya (PM), Ethan (DevOps)

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect): go over function calling integration, fix 3 bad JSON outputs, confirm SDK pattern for tool calls, plan perf run.

[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick roll call. we've got about 45 minutes. Samir's going to walk through the SDK snippets and then we'll dig into the three failing cases Maria sent.
[00:12] Maria: sounds good, and thanks, yes the three cases are in the pilot channel and in the spreadsheet. two are structured output malformations, one is a latency timeout.
[00:20] Samir: cool. quick context: we're assuming you're using the Redwood hosted endpoint in staging with the SDK. the function calling is enabled, and for these tests we turned on structured output mode so the model returns JSON with the schema we defined. there are a few patterns we recommend — let me share my screen in a sec.
[00:36] Tom: one question off the bat: is structured output enforced server-side or just a soft suggestion to the model? sometimes we see the model forget a field.
[00:45] Samir: good call. by default Redwood's function-calling is like the open approach — you pass a JSON schema and the model is steered to emit JSON. we also provide post-hoc validators in the SDK that can auto-retry with a schema-aware prompt if the output fails validation. if you need stronger guarantees you can enable strict schema enforcement in the runtime which will attempt re-parsing and, if necessary, return a structured error object rather than free text. that strict path can add a little latency because of retries.
[01:10] Priya: what's the latency hit typically? Maria mentioned one timeout at ~8s which is killing the mobile UX.
[01:18] Samir: in our profiling it depends on model and sequence length — for a 1k token request inline schema enforcement + retry could add 200-400ms average, worst case maybe a second. but that 8s you saw sounds like a client-side timeout; are you streaming?
[01:32] Maria: currently non-streaming, iOS client. we were hoping to stream partial JSON so the UI can render early but maintain schema integrity.
[01:42] Samir: streaming structured JSON is tricky but doable. pattern we suggest: stream the 'envelope' (meta + incremental token stream) and apply local incremental JSON assembly with a lenient parser that waits for closing braces; once schema validated, mark component as final. Redwood SDK has an example where you can subscribe to event chunks and perform a schema-validate-per-chunk approach — we'll send that snippet.
[01:59] Ethan: are there any caveats for using streaming with our mobile networking (intermittent cellular)? will partial chunks create inconsistent states?
[02:08] Samir: you'll need idempotency and rehydration logic on the client. for intermittent networks we recommend small chunk sizes and local buffering, and saving last-good-state so the UI can fall back if stream drops. Samir: also note KV cache — or KV cash in some transcriptions — is best used server-side for repeated prefixes to reduce cost. Rusty speech here.
[02:28] Tom: can you clarify how function calling maps to our backend tools? we have an internal `lookup_user` REST microservice and also a synchronous enrichment pipeline.
[02:36] Samir: absolutely. there are two models: 1) model-as-orchestrator — the LLM returns a function call payload which your runtime executes (we support direct HTTP tool integrations or you can intercept and run custom logic), 2) return structured intent and let backend decide. for sensitive operations you should do the latter and gate via RBAC and SSO.
[02:54] Maria: our concern is user PII. any best practice on not sending full PII to the model?
[03:01] Jules: we recommend redaction and using embedding indexes server-side. for cases where you must include PII, use tokenization+KMS encryption for payloads in transit and at rest. Redwood supports KMS integrations and audit logging; we'll add the security pack doc to the pilot folder.
[03:18] Priya: can you send the specific SDK pattern for function call -> tool execution -> structured response that includes a retry on validation fail?
[03:26] Samir: yes. i'll include two versions: a simple sync flow and a streaming flow with incremental validation. i want to call out the reconciling logic: if the model returns an unknown enum value, prefer to map to 'unknown' rather than failing the whole response. that reduces user-facing errors.
[03:45] Tom: about the three failing cases: case A and B are malformed JSON (extra commas or missing fields) and case C is a high tail latency when the cache miss hits the enrichment pipeline. Maria, do you want to run through logs?
[03:58] Maria: sure. case A: when the product name contains emoji the model sometimes adds stray characters and the JSON parser fails. see log snippet 1 in the channel.
[04:10] Samir: emoji can confuse tokenization — workaround is to pre-normalize or replace emoji with placeholder tokens server-side before sending prompt. we have a small helper in the SDK for that.
[04:20] Maria: good. case B is the model returning an extra nested array when we expected an object — looks like occasional hallucination.
[04:29] Samir: for that we recommend schema-on-send with a prompt-template that enumerates examples; also use the SDK's 'validate-and-reprompt' helper which will retry up to N times and then return structured error. we'll attach a sample that shows three-shot steering.
[04:43] Priya: what's your recommendation if retries still fail in production? degrade gracefully?
[04:49] Samir: yes degrade: return fallback UI with manual review queue or cached previous result. you can also return partial structured data and flag missing fields for background enrichment.
[04:59] Lena: quick note for product: we saw a few customers prefer returning a predictable error object to the client so the app can handle retries itself. that pattern reduces surprises.
[05:10] Ethan: on the infra side, for case C the tail latency, could Dedicated pool help? our enrichment pipeline is external; sometimes model + enrichment step serializes to high latency.
[05:21] Samir: Dedicated helps reduce variance at the model stage, less noisy neighbors and predictable p99 for the LLM inference. but if your enrichment step is the dominant cost you'll want to parallelize or move enrichment upstream. also consider caching enrichment results keyed by stable user+context.
[05:36] Tom: what's the best way to benchmark end-to-end? we want a number representative of mobile 3G conditions and also a med-tier WiFi baseline.
[05:44] Jules: we recommend running two perf suites: 1) synthetic load against the Dedicated staging endpoint with controlled concurrency to measure LLM latency p50/p95/p99, 2) end-to-end tests from a runner in the cloud that simulates network conditions (tc/netem) to capture client-to-client latency including enrichment. we'll help set the Dedicated staging pool for you.
[06:05] Maria: if we do the staging perf run, what telemetry should we send back?
[06:11] Samir: send token counts, model variant, streaming vs non-streaming, full request id, and tracing spans. Redwood injects tracer headers if you enable distributed tracing in the SDK. also include the rejected JSON payloads and the raw model outputs for debug.
[06:26] Priya: we talked internally about switching to a smaller quantized variant to cut cost. any caveats for structure output on quantized models?
[06:33] Samir: quantization can slightly increase hallucination rate for edge cases but it's mostly workload dependent. structured schema plus validate-and-reprompt mitigates. Redwood Optimize will make a recommendation based on your actual prompt set; we'll feed your pilot prompts into the Optimize tool and report recommended quantization/profile.
[06:52] Tom: do you have a recommended token budget for mobile interactions? we want to cap cost to predictable levels.
[06:58] Jules: set a per-request token cap and a monthly project budget; the SDK supports per-request token limits and will truncate/shorten prompts accordingly. we'll compute cost-per-1000-interactions estimate once we get sample prompt distribution.
[07:12] Maria: back to integration: Samir can you walk through the actual SDK call we should use? maybe paste pseudo-code.
[07:19] Samir: sure — high level: 1) construct prompt + schema 2) call redwood.sdk.generate({model, schema, streaming: true/false, tools: ["lookup_user"], idempotencyKey}) 3) if streaming subscribe to onChunk and assemble json 4) on final, run schema validator 5) if invalid, call reprompt with clarifying instruction. i'll paste the annotated snippet in the pilot channel.
[07:42] Maria: will the SDK automatically call our internal REST tool if we register it? we don't want to expose it publicly.
[07:49] Samir: you register tools in your backend and pass tool descriptors in the SDK call. the SDK doesn't call external services on Redwood's hosted environment unless you use Redwood-managed integrations; if you register a tool with a private endpoint it remains inside your vpc or private bridge — for hosted trials we recommend keeping the tool execution in your environment and just handing the model the function signature.
[08:10] Ethan: what about auth between Redwood and our tool?
[08:14] Samir: for private tools use signed tokens and short-lived certs; for Dedicated or Private deployments you can set up mutual TLS or a sidecar bridge. we'll share the docs.
[08:24] Maria: okay good. small transcription noise: i saw a mention of 'prefix caching' — is that the same as the KV cache?
[08:31] Samir: yes prefix caching stored in a KV store, shortened to KV cash sometimes by the transcription gods. that cache reduces repeated computation for identical prefixes — helpful for chatty prompts.
[08:41] Priya: let's talk about observability — after we push the SDK will we see token-level breakdowns and per-route latency?
[08:47] Jules: yes, Redwood Console will show per-route token breakdown, p50/p95/p99 and error rates. we'll flag validation-fail counts as a separate metric so you can tune prompts and schema.
[08:59] Tom: before we wrap, any changes to the POC acceptance criteria based on today's chat?
[09:04] Lena: i'd propose small tweak: acceptance includes 1) successful integration of streaming structured output in the mobile flow for at least 3 representative screens with <2% validation failures, 2) p95 end-to-end latency under 2.5s on the WiFi baseline, and 3) documented fallback path for PII redaction. ok with everyone?
[09:22] Priya: yes that's reasonable.
[09:24] Maria: yes, we'll try to hit that and post results.
[09:28] Samir: action items as we listed. i'll drop the SDK snippet and a strict vs lenient enforcement matrix. also sending the security integration doc and Dedicated staging request form.
[09:39] Lena: great, thanks all. next check-in same time next week?
[09:44] Maria: works for me.
[09:46] Tom: fine.
[09:48] Jules: i'll send calendar invite.

End of transcript.
